result.title: SpikePose: Lightweight Video Human Pose Estimation
result.summary: Efficient video human pose estimation must balance localisation accuracy, motion quality, and energy cost. We present SpikePose, a lightweight video pose estimator that pairs a frame-reset, single-step spiking encoder with motion-aligned heatmap memory (MAM). The encoder supplies per-frame spatial evidence, while MAM estimates joint displacement, aligns historical heatmaps, and adaptively fuses them with current predictions. By confining temporal reasoning to a compact, lightweight module outside the spiking backbone, SpikePose helps bridge the gap between spiking and classical Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) on large-scale, non-event-driven video tasks. We evaluate spatial accuracy, motion errors, and estimated arithmetic energy on MPII and a fixed NTU60 Cross-Subject subset. Against the architecture-matched ANN with MAM, SpikePose cuts estimated arithmetic energy by 91.4% at a cost of just 1.12 points in head-bone-normalised PCK at 0.5 threshold (PCK_HB(0.5)). Within SpikePose, adding MAM reduces velocity and acceleration errors by 28.13% and 31.46% while slightly improving localisation, at a cost of only 0.003M parameters and 0.0023 analytical GFLOPs per frame. Code will be released on GitHub upon acceptance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SpikePose，将帧重置的单步脉冲编码器用于逐帧空间证据提取，并配运动对齐热图记忆（MAM）估计关节位移、对齐历史热图并与当前预测自适应融合，在 MPII 与 NTU60 子集上比较定位精度、运动误差和估算能耗。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 MAM 先按估计位移对齐历史热图再加权融合，可供核查 LVR 中跨推理步 latent 状态的对齐、历史证据保留与筛选；其解析能耗/精度权衡也可供参考迭代式 THINK/LOOK 的成本度量，但任务为视频人体姿态估计、无显式推理与答案使用机制，迁移仅为推测。
